tube-noise.look: 3D at 5% air: clean worm tunnels of near constant round section, tangled and looping, with almost no flanges. Side by side on the same channels the abs+abs, max and length recipes are flanged webs and this is tubes. Plain mode gives separate loops rather than a network, with an occasional flat lens where two zero surfaces nearly touch and one straight rod on seed 1337. R from 0.05 to 0.2 stays tubular, R=0.35 merges into blobs. Network mode (3 channels, min over pairs) gives a dense connected tangle. World-unit roughness gives lumpy cave or worm-coral walls. 2D codim 1: truly constant width wandering lines, relief reads as constant width canyons. 2D codim 2: small irregular dots, not very interesting.
tube-noise.dims: 2D (codim 1 lines c0ratio 7.40), 3D (tilted plane c0ratio 7.85), 4D (c0ratio 7.16 with w as time; xyz-only Jacobian looks cleaner than full 4D). Torus-mapped tile test runs and looks fine, seamlessness judged by eye only.
tube-noise.range: Tunnel output clamped to [-1,1], +1 on the centre line, 0 at the wall. Measured -1.000 to 0.996 over 8 seeds.
tube-noise.artifacts: Same-lattice channels pass through every lattice point: 2D Perlin shows an integer grid of dots, simplex large blobs at kernel gaps. Fixed by a per-vertex value term at one lattice. Residual: flat lenses where gradients are near parallel, false air about 1%. Tangent rejection (s0) shredded the tubes, rejected. One refine step: r_CV .239 to .205 at L=.5, doubles cost, not worth it. Radius varies under warp unless it is chain-ruled: unchained warp visibly varies, finite differences stay uniform. 2D codim 1 lines get small dark slits at saddles.
tube-noise.node_shape: TubeNoise: Mode enum {Tube, Network, Sheet}; Output enum {Tunnel, Distance, Pipe, Rope, plus Length, MaxAbs, AbsAdd}; Radius hybrid in feature units (default about 0.1); Damping float (default 0.02); Feature Scale; Seed Offset; Output Min/Max. A generic two-source form with finite differences is a separate question: scalar 301.7 ns vs 100.4 ns analytic.
tube-noise.port_notes: One Perlin lattice visit, two 16-entry gradient lookups from hash bit slices, 4-bit value from high bits, value and Jacobian accumulated together. No window. Branch-free algebra, one division and one Sqrt. Network adds a third channel and two more 2x2 solves sharing dot products; scalar 117.4 vs 100.4 ns. Damping is in units of gradient squared, keep it in noise space after Feature Scale. scalar_vs_perlin is the 3D run; 2D and 4D are 1.24 and 10.28. At 5% air on Perlin + value: radius CV .132 vs .360 for abs+abs, aspect 1.30 vs 2.38, blowouts 2.5% vs 19.9%, false air 1.1% vs 13.3%, largest air component 28% vs 87%, network 90%.

critic.notes: Verified: c0ratio 7.05 (3D plane), range -1..0.993, far coords clean, scalar 3D 2.01x perlin2 (99 ns), network 2.29x (118 ns), 4D 10.3x (527 ns). Seed 42 at window 8 looks like the seed 1337 window 4 images: round-section worm tangle, no lattice, flake debris present in both tube and net3. The real abs+abs graph rendered through fnlab at the same air fraction and seed is flanged ribbon-sheets, so the comparison is honest and the look cannot be had from existing nodes because every |n| recipe scales width with the local gradient. Costs: plain tubes are separate closed loops (37% largest air component at 5% air in the prototyper table), network mode is the usable cave mode, junctions widen the section, 2D codim-2 output is dull dots, and 4D is heavy (16 corners, 2-3 channels with Jacobians), so GenTileable2D will be slow; my 4D AVX2 estimate is 20-40 ns, not 7-12. Ship as TubeNoise with Mode {Tube, Network}, Output {Tunnel, Distance, Pipe}; Rope is a showcase output needing an atan2 approximation; Length/MaxAbs are free by-products only.

master.one_liner: Turns 1, 2 or 3 source fields into a first-order true distance to their common zero set, so spaghetti caves get uniform tube radius and cheese walls uniform thickness.
master.look:
Prototyped against the plain sqrt(f^2+g^2) Minecraft form using an isosurface render, and the difference is large: the plain form bulges into webs and sheet-like blobs where gradients are weak, while this one gives clean worm tubes of near constant radius tangled through the volume. 2D: small near-round dots at zero crossings. 3D slice: ellipses and elongated dashes. Also gives constant-thickness sponge walls from 1 source, and a cheap Lipschitz-normalised field for sphere tracing.
[TubeNoise, volumetric-3d4d] 3D iso-surface: a tangle of smooth near-constant-diameter worm tunnels that bend, pass over and under each other and branch at saddle points, with no dead ends (level-set intersections are closed 1-manifolds). With FBm-warped input the tubes wriggle. 2D slice: round discs of similar diameter, a few elongated where a tube grazes the plane; with w the discs drift, merge and split as tubes sweep through. Codim-1 mode: uniform-width sheets (cheese/sheet caves) or 2D river networks.
master.algorithm:
Sources f (and g, h). Gradients by forward differences at Epsilon, or analytically in a built-in Perlin variant. Gauss-Newton distance with Levenberg damping, 1 source: d = |f| / sqrt(|grad f|^2 + L). 2 sources: a = grad f . grad f, b = grad f . grad g, c = grad g . grad g, det = (a+L)(c+L) - b^2, d^2 = ((c+L) f^2 - 2 b f g + (a+L) g^2) / det. 3 sources: the same with the 3x3 inverse by cofactors. Output ScaleOutput(min(d, Dmax), 0, Dmax), optionally minus Radius (hybrid). Damping is the key detail: with a det+eps form, d goes to 0 at critical points and creates false tunnels, while with G+L*I, d^2 goes to |f|^2/L, which is large, so rock stays rock. Codimension 2 in 3D gives curves, in 2D isolated points, in 4D surfaces.

[TubeNoise, volumetric-3d4d] One Perlin lattice visit (8 corners in 3D, 16 in 4D). Per corner hash h: two independent gradients g1 = Grad[h & 15], g2 = Grad[(h >> 4) & 15]. Compute n1, n2 by quintic-interpolated gradient dots AND their analytic gradients G1 = grad n1, G2 = grad n2 (standard Perlin-with-derivatives: value = a + u(b-a) + v(c-a) + w(e-a) + ... ; derivative = lerped corner gradients + du*(corner differences), du = 30 f^2 (f-1)^2). In 4D take only the x,y,z partials (w is time).
 a = G1.G1, c = G2.G2, b = G1.G2
 d2 = (c*n1*n1 - 2*b*n1*n2 + a*n2*n2) / max(a*c - b*b, eps)   // n^T (J J^T)^-1 n, first-order distance to the codim-2 set
 d  = Min( Sqrt(d2), MaxDist )
Outputs (enum): Tunnel = 1 - 2*Min(d/Radius, 1) (inside = +1), Distance = signed (d - Radius), Phase = n1 * InvSqrt(n1^2+n2^2+eps) (angle-like coordinate around the tube, for stripes/ribs along tunnels). Codim param (int 1..3, default 2): codim 1 uses only n1 -> d = |n1|/|G1| (constant-thickness sheets / rivers in 2D), codim 3 adds n3 -> isolated blobs. 2D with codim 2 gives dots (the curve pierces the plane); 2D default should be codim 1 (wandering rivers/cracks).
master.why_new: The known spaghetti recipe has pinches and blowouts because thickness depends on local noise gradient, and no graph can cure that (no gradient node exists; a hand-built graph would have dozens of duplicated nodes). Works with any source, including warped fractals, and output is in world units so Radius is meaningful. Makes a hard thing easy rather than adding a new texture.
master.simd_plan:
Perlin.inl-style per-dimension Gen, second gradient set from spare hash bits, derivative accumulation alongside the value (about 2x the FMAs). All branch-free; one Sqrt, one Reciprocal. Est. 2.5-3x Perlin: ~3 ns 2D, ~6 ns 3D, ~13 ns 4D (vs 12/41 for Cellular). 4D is exact (true 4D lattice), so GenTileable2D works.
[LevelSetDistance, volumetric-3d4d] No loop or window. Sources evaluated (1+dim) times each: 3D with 2 sources is 8 evals, 8 x 2.2 = 18 ns for Perlin, plus about 1 ns algebra. An analytic Perlin3 pair built in costs about 7 ns. 4D: 10 evals, 43 ns with Perlin. Tetrahedral gradient has no benefit here. Branch free.
master.continuity: Inherits the source's smoothness (C1 to C2 for Perlin) apart from the first-order min with Dmax, which is C0 and only far from the tube. d itself has a cone point at the centre line only, matching a true distance.
master.params: Codimension via 1 to 3 GeneratorSource inputs, Epsilon (float), Damping L (float), Dmax (float), Radius (hybrid). Variant enum for built-in Perlin pair with analytic gradients.
master.risks:
Estimate is only trustworthy near the zero set: at 0.6 units the 2D dots turn into teardrops, so keep Dmax near 2 to 3 radii. Cost 8x Perlin if generic. Epsilon must scale with source Feature Scale, or use a world-unit default. Near-tangent crossings of f and g produce short dashes rather than round tubes.
[TubeDistance, libs-modifiers] All gradient noises are zero at their own lattice points, so two same-lattice sources make a regular grid of fake dots (observed before adding kOffset; seen clearly in the wide view). Thin specks remain where gradients are nearly parallel. In 2D the output is only dots, so the value is mostly 3D. The real SIMD eps value needs tuning for source scale.
sources: from memory, not consulted: Minecraft 1.18 'spaghetti caves' (|n1|<t && |n2|<t); Taubin 1994 first-order distance estimate
master.cost_note: Perlin.inl-style per-dimension Gen, second gradient set from spare hash bits, derivative accumulation alongside the value (about 2x the FMAs). 2.5-3x Perlin: ~3 ns 2D, ~6 ns 3D, ~13 ns 4D (vs 12/41 for Cellular).
master.variant_notes: Levenberg damping is the key detail: det+eps creates false tunnels at critical points. Same-lattice sources make a grid of fake dots unless offset by a non-lattice constant. The analytic built-in form is much cheaper and offers phase around the tube.

tpms-noise.look: All seven families render as correct-looking labyrinths, though their feature sizes differ a lot at the same period and would need normalising. Plain gyroid is obviously a crystal. With a Perlin warp of 6.6 rad at 0.157 cycles per unit it turns into a smooth organic sponge with rounded saddle walls, visibly smoother and more connected than Perlin or Simplex thresholded at 0, which are craggy with thin sheets and fragments. Cut at a high level it is a warped srs net: a bone or foam skeleton with three-way junctions, the only base here that looks grown rather than tangled. Warp of 1.5 to 3 rad still reads as a bent lattice. Warp too fast (wf 0.6) shreds into fine lamellae. 2D slices are stripe and maze patterns and the relief is unremarkable: this is a 3D node. Raw sheet mode already looks near uniform in thickness, so the |g|/|grad g| form adds little on gyroid.
tpms-noise.dims: 2D, 3D, 4D all measured continuous, c0ratio 8.00 each with the Perlin warp. 4D phase orbit keeps the gyroid at all w. Torus-mapped tile test: orbit looks usable, the G4 alternative looks worse.

IWP measured -5..3, so the idea's 6 is not tight, and Lidinoid -1.35..1.15. Both are asymmetric and want a remap to fill [-1,1]. Warped gyroid measured -1.000 to 1.000.
tpms-noise.artifacts: FFT keeps an axis cross after warp: axis stat at window 16 is 45 plain, 37 one octave, 10 two octaves; it is window dependent, the window 8 sheet reads 48. Bounded warp leaves a constant periodic residue at every lag until a reaches about 3 rad (Simplex warp wf .25: a=1 ac .68, a=2 ac .20, a=4 ac 0). Simplex 3D warp gives c0ratio 4.2, Perlin 8.0. Seeds only translate the pattern when no warp is plugged in.

master.one_liner: Triply periodic minimal surface family (Gyroid, Schwarz P/D, Neovius, IWP, Lidinoid, Fischer-Koch) as a generator with per-axis hybrid phase, sheet mode and a w-driven phase orbit; the only field whose iso-surfaces are guaranteed bicontinuous labyrinths.
master.look:
3D iso-surface at 0: the classic gyroid/Schwarz labyrinths, two interpenetrating connected tunnel systems with saddle-shaped walls; squash with DomainAxisScale for flattened cavern layers that stay connected; warp with FBm via the phase hybrids for organic sponge, trabecular bone, coral skeleton, foam sheets. Sheet mode iso-surfaces are uniform-thickness curved walls (membranes). 2D slice: a maze of wavy stripes and hooks (gyroid) or a dot/ring lattice (SchwarzP); with phase noise it looks like lamellar bone or brain coral.
[TPMSMorph, volumetric-3d4d] Prototyped with th varied by Perlin at mf 0.5. 3D isosurface: a gyroid-like lattice that distorts from one motif to another across space, staying a connected sponge with no pinches. 2D slice: warped wave and diamond motifs. Good for sci-fi lattices, coral, bone scaffold, alien architecture, grown metal. With warp source upstream it becomes organic gyroid noise.
master.algorithm:
p *= 2*pi/FeatureScale (ScalableGenerator). Add hybrid phases: x += PhaseX(p), y += PhaseY(p), z += PhaseZ(p) (hybrids, default 0; feeding FBm Simplex here is the 'gyroid noise' sponge). 4D: additionally x += (pi/2)*sin(w), y += (pi/2)*sin(w+2.094), z += (pi/2)*sin(w+4.189) so the surface flows along its own screw axes and loops with period 2*pi in w. Compute sx,cx,sy,cy,sz,cz = Sin/Cos of x,y,z (6 trig). Family enum:
  Gyroid    g = sx*cy + sy*cz + sz*cx                  (|g|<=1.5)
  SchwarzP  g = cx + cy + cz                          (3)
  SchwarzD  g = sx*sy*sz + sx*cy*cz + cx*sy*cz + cx*cy*sz (1)
  Neovius   g = 3(cx+cy+cz) + 4 cx*cy*cz              (13)
  IWP       g = 2(cx*cy + cy*cz + cz*cx) - (c2x+c2y+c2z), c2x = 1-2sx*sx (6)
  Lidinoid  g = 0.5(s2x*cy*sz + s2y*cz*sx + s2z*cx*sy) - 0.5(c2x*c2y + c2y*c2z + c2z*c2x) + 0.15, s2x = 2 sx cx
  FischerKochS g = c2x*sy*cz + c2y*sz*cx + c2z*sx*cy
Output enum: Signed = g/gmax; Sheet = 1 - |g|/gmax (double-walled thin shell; threshold = wall thickness); Channel = Abs flipped. 2D: z = PhaseZ hybrid (default 0), i.e. a slice. Normalise by the per-family analytic max (table).

[TPMSMorph, volumetric-3d4d] Scaled coords X=f*x etc, with six sin/cos. G = sX cY + sY cZ + sZ cX; D = cX cY cZ - sX sY sZ; P = (cX+cY+cZ)/1.5. F = cos(th)*D + sin(th)*G, with th(p) a hybrid (Bonnet-style association by nodal approximations), with an optional second lerp toward P. Output enum: Solid F-Offset, Sheet |F-Offset|-Wall. Offset and Wall hybrids give density grading. Divide by a local gradient estimate is unnecessary since |grad F| is bounded by about sqrt(3) f and is analytic, giving a Lipschitz field ideal for sphere tracing. 4D: G4 = sX cY + sY cZ + sZ cW + sW cX with an analogous D4, a real 4D periodic field whose slices morph and loop over w period 2 pi and support GenTileable. For cheaper loops, th = base + omega*w gives D to G to -D to -G. 2D form is the z=0 slice.
master.why_new: Not expressible: SineWave is sin(x)sin(y)sin(z) only, no mixed sin*cos sums. Delivers caves/sponge with guaranteed connectivity of both phases (gyroid level sets for |t| < ~1.41 of 1.5 keep both labyrinths connected), zero-mean-curvature look, tileable by construction, C-infinity, and w-phase looping animation at 3D cost. Phase hybrids give in-node per-axis domain warp.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free, no lattice/window: 6 Sin/Cos (+3 Sin in 4D) plus ~15 FMAs; family switch is a node-level enum compiled per Gen (or Select over all families, still cheap). GenT over the pack: 2D drops z to a hybrid. Cost ~0.7x Perlin 3D, ~1x Perlin 4D. Hybrid phases cost whatever is plugged in.
master.continuity: C-infinity (sums of products of sines). Sheet mode has a C0 crease at g=0 (intended).
master.params: Family enum; Output enum (Signed/Sheet); Phase X/Y/Z hybrid (default 0); Feature Scale; Phase Speed W (float, 4D only); Output Min/Max.
master.risks:
Pure TPMS is visibly periodic; it needs a warp or the phase hybrids to look natural (document a default recipe). Normalisation maxima for Lidinoid/Neovius are tabulated constants, not exact. Both-phases-connected guarantee weakens under strong warps.
[TPMSMorph, volumetric-3d4d] Regular without inputs; seeds only shift phases. Interpolated nodal forms are approximations of true Bonnet associates, so intermediate surfaces are not minimal. The w=0 slice of G4 is not exactly a gyroid. Far coordinates: Sin accuracy at large arguments needs checking.
master.variant_notes: Family enum plus hybrid phase warp, with TPMSMorph's hybrid Bonnet-angle blend so topology family flows across space. Interpolated forms are nodal approximations, not true minimal surfaces.

vector-simplex-length.look: Saw three things. 2D, shared lattice as written (lat=0): a triangular grid of small ring-and-dot basins at the simplex vertices and a strong X in the FFT, not the promised lattice-free pebbles. 3D Length at 5% air: flanged, webbed ribbons, with big sheet-like blobs where the simplex kernels leave gaps and both channels fade together. Length is not rounder than Max or abs+abs in any way that matters, the flanges stay. Perlin channels with the value term look close to the two-noise graph. C=3 gives lumpy blobs, not round pockets, at the thresholds tried.
vector-simplex-length.dims: 2D, 3D, 4D all run and measured continuous: c0ratio 8.01 / 7.98 / 7.99
vector-simplex-length.range: Channels near [-1,1] with lat=0 (max 0.996). Value term raises channel max to 1.40 (vamp .15), so the normaliser must be re-measured. Length is not normalised in the prototype: mode=5 reached 2.9.
vector-simplex-length.artifacts: Simplex kernels are shorter than the vertex spacing, so every gradient channel is exactly 0 at every vertex and the shared-lattice zero set threads the lattice: pierce density 11.73 vs 6.06 per unit^2 for two lattices. Shared amplitude envelope: corr(|n1|,|n2|) +0.143 vs -0.013, near-zero volume 1.85x. Value correlation from bit slices is fine, |corr| < 0.01. False air at the same air fraction: 20.5% shared, 17.4% value term, 8.7% two lattices. Perlin shares far better: corr +0.012 with value .35, false air 11.9% vs 11.4%.
vector-simplex-length.node_shape: No separate node. Output modes Length, MaxAbs, AbsAdd on the TubeNoise kernel, using Perlin value-term channels. The one-lattice multi-channel kernel is worth keeping as a shared internal, TPMS warp uses it too.
vector-simplex-length.port_notes: Cost claim holds: scalar 1.01x one simplex for lat=0, 1.11x with value term, 1.74x for two lattices. Saving about 2.8 ns per 3D sample (estimate) against the measured 5.17 ns graph. No look gain over that graph, and the simplex form is visibly worse. scalar_vs_perlin is the 3D run; 2D and 4D are 0.97 and 4.76.

critic.params: lat=1,mode=0,f=0.5 (channel source); Length only as a by-product output of the TubeNoise Perlin kernel
critic.notes: Agree with the merge. The idea as pitched (lattice-free pebbles from one simplex traversal) failed on the prototyper's own sheets: the shared-lattice simplex form is a triangular grid of dots with an X in the FFT, and the 3D Length cut is flanged sheets no rounder than abs+abs. The Perlin + value-term form only reproduces the two-noise graph a bit cheaper. What survives is the shared one-lattice multi-channel kernel with the per-vertex value term, which TubeNoise needs anyway. Length and MaxAbs cost nothing extra there, so keep them as optional outputs; if the Output enum gets crowded they are the first to cut. No separate node.

master.one_liner: Multi-channel simplex from one lattice pass with vector outputs reduced to a scalar: |v| gives worm tunnels (Minecraft spaghetti/noodle caves, ore veins) in 3D and lattice-free pebble basins in 2D; MaxAbs reproduces Minecraft's exact cave formula at half the cost.
master.look: 3D: continuous winding tunnels of controllable diameter that branch and merge where channels cross zero together (spaghetti caves), finer 'noodle' version at higher frequency, or spherical pockets (cheese holes) with C=3. 2D: a cellular-like field of round basins with Gaussian spacing and no lattice regularity, smoother than Worley F1.
master.algorithm: Single OpenSimplex2 traversal; at each contributing vertex take the 32-bit hash and derive C (2..4) independent gradient indices by multiplying the hash with distinct odd constants and taking top bits (or bit slices); the falloff (a^4) is computed once, each channel adds falloff*(g_c . d). Channels n_1..n_C, each normalised like Simplex. Output enum: Length sqrt(sum n_c^2) (2D C=2: zero set = isolated points -> smooth round basins; 3D C=2: zero set = curves -> tubes; 3D C=3: zero set = points -> pockets); MaxAbs max_c |n_c| (Minecraft: max(|S1|,|S2|) with thresholds -0.0765 - 0.0115*thickness); MinAbs; Channel i (cheap decorrelated noise for graphs sharing a lattice); Tube: 1 - Length/Thickness (hybrid Thickness; Minecraft's thickness modulator) clamped to [-1,1]. Rarity (Minecraft interval_select on scale) is achieved by wrapping in DomainScale, or expose a hybrid Scale Multiplier evaluated per lane (per-lane frequency: continuous if the controlling field is smooth).
master.why_new: The graph equivalent (two Simplex nodes, Abs, Max) costs two full noise evaluations; the shared lattice version costs ~1.2x one. Length (Euclidean cross-section) gives round tubes that Max(|a|,|b|) cannot. Minecraft 1.18's cave system is the most copied recent world-gen design and FastNoise is routinely used to clone it.
master.simd_plan: Simplex cost + (C-1) dot products and accumulations per vertex (3 vertices 2D, 4 in 3D, 5 in 4D) + one Sqrt: ~1.15x (C=2) to 1.4x (C=4) Simplex in all dimensions. Gradient index derivation from one hash: 2 integer multiplies per extra channel. GenT friendly (reuse Simplex.inl with a channel loop).
master.continuity: Channels are C2; Length is C0 at the zero set only (|v| cusp, which is the tunnel centre line, harmless after thresholding); MaxAbs C0 at channel crossings; Tube C0 where clamped.
master.params: Channels (int 2..4), Output enum {Length, MaxAbs, MinAbs, Channel, Tube}, Channel Index, Thickness (hybrid), Feature Scale, Seed Offset.
master.risks: Channels from one hash are correlated if bit extraction is sloppy (test with FFT and cross-correlation); tubes pinch to zero diameter where only one channel is zero and the other is small (same as Minecraft, acceptable).
master.cost_note: Simplex cost + (C-1) dot products and accumulations per vertex (3 vertices 2D, 4 in 3D, 5 in 4D) + one Sqrt: ~1.15x (C=2) to 1.4x (C=4) Simplex in all dimensions.
